summary: Lookout cabin built in 1946 and reported staffed in 1946-47, per a register that quotes period newsletter and newspaper items; later fate not found.

facts.design: Cabin about 4.3 m (14 ft) square, built almost entirely by the lookoutman; fire finder in the centre of the room

events.note: Built in the 1946 season; work began in June and the cabin was occupied in early July.
Occupied in early July 1946 by lookoutman Charles Egg and his family.
A Daily Colonist item dated June 3, 1947, as quoted on the register page, reports Mr. and Mrs. Neil Magee on duty at the lookout.

evidence.quote: This point was developed as a lookout during the 1946 season.

evidence.supports: Work began in June; cabin occupied in early July
evidence.quote: Despite the fact that development of this point did not commence until June, the building was occupied in early July

evidence.supports: Tractor road; lumber from an old camp; windows from Victoria; district supplied hardware and shingles
evidence.quote: A tractor road was bulldozed to the site, lumber was obtained from the remains of an old A.S.W. Camp, windows from the property Clerk, Victoria, and the district provided hardware and shingles to complete the job.

evidence.supports: Newsletter item names the Forest Branch
Lookout placed in the Vancouver Forest District
evidence.quote: the construction of the Bowser Lookout in the Vancouver Forest District during 1946

evidence.supports: Cabin about 14 ft square; bunks, tables, cupboards and stove under the windows
evidence.quote: The building is approximately 14 feet square, and, built along the four sides of the room underneath the windows are bunks, tables, cupboards and a stove.

evidence.supports: Fire finder in the centre of the room; unobstructed view
evidence.quote: The fire finder is located in the centre of the room and an unobstructed view is maintained in all directions.

evidence.supports: Built almost entirely by the lookoutman in about twenty man-days
evidence.quote: The building was constructed almost entirely by the lookoutman himself, and about twenty man days of labour were required to make the place habitable.

evidence.supports: Cost about $100; called a temporary lookout
evidence.quote: for the expenditure of about $100, constructed a temporary lookout of excellent design

evidence.supports: Lookoutman Charles Egg, a recently discharged veteran, affected by illness from service
evidence.quote: Lookoutman Charles Egg, a recently discharged veteran, is handicapped by the effects of illness contracted during his service.

evidence.supports: Lookoutman and his family comfortably housed in the building
evidence.quote: A well constructed building resulted in which are comfortably located the Lookoutman and his family.

evidence.supports: Daily Colonist item of June 3, 1947: Mr. and Mrs. Neil Magee on duty
evidence.quote: Mr. and Mrs. Neil Magee are on duty at the Bowser lookout.

evidence.supports: Register heading gives the area as Nanaimo
Community of Bowser is in the Regional District of Nanaimo
evidence.quote: Bowser is in the Regional District of Nanaimo

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register heading names Nanaimo, while the 1946 newsletter item places the lookout in the Vancouver Forest District. The two labels name different kinds of place and the register does not say how they relate, so the story gives both as the sources state them.

notes_for_editor: The 1946 construction and 1946-47 staffing details come from one register page that quotes a Forest Branch News Letter item (November 1, 1946) and a Daily Colonist item (June 3, 1947). I could not see the originals. The newspaper and newsletter are the best next check: the Daily Colonist is searchable through BC newspaper archives. No source I read gives the lookout's fate or present condition, and status and access remain unknown. Register coordinates (49.422, -124.766) and elevation (389, no unit printed) match the brief. Unused lead: a DualSportBC forum thread titled Bowser Forest Look Out appeared in search results; the forum returned HTTP 403, so its text was not read. It may describe the tower in later years, so check it before adding any later history. Unresolved: the register heading Nanaimo versus the newsletter's Vancouver Forest District. The brief has no local_unit for this tower, so no correction is proposed.
